title: How to end your thread in cross-stitch
subtitle: Finishing a thread without a knot on the back
excerpt: A cross-stitch thread ends by weaving the tail under existing stitches on the back of the fabric. No knot, no bump. Four to six stitches woven in a figure-of-eight pattern hold the thread permanently.
sourceNotes: Standard knot-free finishing method documented in Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), Project Gutenberg #20776. Also in Weldon's Practical Needlework (1880s), Internet Archive.

glossaryTerms.definition: The knot-free method of finishing a thread in cross-stitch. The tail is woven under existing stitches on the back of the fabric in a figure-of-eight pattern, securing it without a bump. The excess is trimmed to within two to three millimetres.

content.text: A cross-stitch thread ends by weaving the tail under the stitches already on the back of the fabric. The same principle that applies to
applies here: no knot. A knot creates a bump that shows through the front of the finished piece. Weaving in the tail under four to six stitches holds it permanently.
The rule for cross-stitch finishing is: weave under at least four stitches, change direction once, trim to two to three millimetres. That combination holds even with washing and handling.
Flip the work to the back.
When the last stitch is in, turn the fabric over so the back is facing you. Thread the needle with the short tail that remains.
Slide the needle under nearby stitches.

Pass the needle under four to six cross-stitch threads that run across the back. Move in one direction, pulling the thread through snugly but not pulling so hard it distorts the stitches on the front.
Turn the needle and weave through two to three more stitches in the opposite direction. This figure-of-eight locks the thread so it cannot pull back out.
Snip the remaining tail to within two to three millimetres of the last stitch you wove under. Too long and it creates a bump; too short and the thread can work free over time.

items.symptom: The tail works free after washing
items.cause: Too few stitches were woven under, or the figure-of-eight turn was skipped.
items.fix: Re-thread the tail and weave under at least four stitches, then change direction for two more. The direction change is what holds; linear weaving alone can slip back out.

items.symptom: The front of the piece pulls into a bump at the finish point
items.cause: The tail was pulled too tightly while weaving.
items.fix: Ease the tension as you weave. The tail should lie flat against the back threads, not dig into them.

items.symptom: The tail is visible through the front of the fabric
items.cause: The weaving path crossed to the front of the fabric.
items.fix: Stay on the back of the work. The needle should only pass under threads that are already on the back, never through to the front.
